sentences.text: Sytten mai: flagg, is og pølse.
sentences.english: The seventeenth of May: flags, ice cream and sausage.

sentences.text: Sytten mai er en stor dag i Norge. Folk feirer at Norge er et land.
sentences.english: The seventeenth of May is a big day in Norway. People celebrate that Norway is a country.

sentences.text: Mange folk har flagg. Mange går i tog i byen.
sentences.english: Many people have flags. Many walk in a parade in town.

sentences.text: Toget går til sentrum, og folk synger.
sentences.english: The parade goes to the town centre, and people sing.

sentences.text: Mange har bunad. Bunaden er gammel og dyr.
sentences.english: Many people wear a bunad. The bunad is old and expensive.

sentences.text: Folk spiser is og pølse. Alle er glade.
sentences.english: People eat ice cream and sausage. Everyone is happy.

sentences.text: Det er sytten mai. Sam står opp tidlig. Det regner ikke, og sola er ute.
sentences.english: It is the seventeenth of May. Sam gets up early. It is not raining, and the sun is out.

sentences.text: Anna har bunad. Hun er glad i bunaden.
sentences.english: Anna has a bunad. She is fond of the bunad.

sentences.text: Lars har flagg, og Nils har flagg også.
sentences.english: Lars has a flag, and Nils has a flag too.

sentences.text: Se toget! Folk synger!
sentences.english: Look at the parade! People are singing!
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Hva synger de?
sentences.english: What are they singing?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: De synger om Norge. Vi feirer at Norge er et land.
sentences.english: They sing about Norway. We celebrate that Norway is a country.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Nils spiser is. Han spiser pølse også. Pølsen er god.
sentences.english: Nils eats ice cream. He eats sausage too. The sausage is good.

sentences.text: Jeg vil ha is. Hvor mye koster den?
sentences.english: I want ice cream. How much does it cost?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Den koster tretti kroner i dag.
sentences.english: It costs thirty kroner today.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Sam spiser, og han er glad.
sentences.english: Sam eats, and he is happy.

sentences.text: Liker du sytten mai, Sam?
sentences.english: Do you like the seventeenth of May, Sam?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Ja! Det er bra å feire. Alle er glade.
sentences.english: Yes! It is good to celebrate. Everyone is happy.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Om kvelden er Sam trøtt. Han sitter hjemme med Anna og Lars.
sentences.english: In the evening Sam is tired. He sits at home with Anna and Lars.

sentences.text: De drikker te, og de snakker om dagen.
sentences.english: They drink tea, and they talk about the day.

sentences.text: Er du glad i Norge, Sam?
sentences.english: Are you fond of Norway, Sam?
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Ja, jeg er veldig glad i Norge. Jeg vil bo her lenge.
sentences.english: Yes, I am very fond of Norway. I want to live here for a long time.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Det er bra. Vi vil ha deg her!
sentences.english: That is good. We want to have you here!
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Jeg tenker på reisen med fly. Jeg pakket ikke mye, og nå har jeg nye venner. Derfor er jeg glad.
sentences.english: I think about the journey by plane. I did not pack much, and now I have new friends. That is why I am glad.

sentences.text: I klassen spør Lars: «Forstår du sytten mai?» Det er et lett spørsmål, men prøven er vanskelig.
sentences.english: In the class Lars asks: "Do you understand the 17th of May?" It is an easy question, but the test is difficult.

sentences.text: Marta er gammel. Hun har levd lenge, og livet var ikke lett på gården.
sentences.english: Marta is old. She has lived a long time, and life was not easy on the farm.
